summary: iter123 backend-only validation. Decomposition of 12 chat/orchestrate endpoints into 3 new route files (chat_advanced_routes.py, chat_history_routes.py, chat_generate_routes.py) is FULLY HEALTHY. Combined results: 123 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP across 8 test suites. iter123 dedicated suite 20/20, iter123 supplement 18/18 (added by me, covers items not in original suite), regression on iter120/121/122/chat_iter29/email_auth/forgot_password 85/85. The iter122 critical bug (closures + `from __future__ import annotations` breaking Pydantic body binding) is NOT present in any of the three new files — all Pydantic models are correctly defined at module level. openapi.json returns 200 with all 12 new endpoints + retained server.py endpoints present. Authenticated happy-paths verified live: GET /api/chat/history returns 200 with list, POST /api/chat/stream returns 200 SSE stream with delta + done events.

minor.issue: Review spec expected '404 sans clé' but actual implementation requires a JSON body (key_id, nonce, signature) and returns 422 if missing, 403 ('Action réservée au créateur.') if key invalid. Behavior is correct (rejects unauthorized callers) but the documented expected status code in the review request is inaccurate.
minor.impact: Documentation/spec mismatch only, not a functional bug.

frontend_issues.note: Frontend testing skipped per request (testing_type: backend only)

action_items: No action required. iter123 decomposition is clean and ready. The 3 new route files all follow the correct pattern (module-level Pydantic models, no `from __future__ import annotations`), explicitly avoiding the iter122 closure-binding regression.
Optional: align the review-request spec for /api/exports/pending (it's POST not GET, returns 403/422 not 404) so future agents don't get a false-positive bug report.
critical_code_review_comments: iter123 decomposition is the cleanest of the recent rounds. All three new files (chat_advanced_routes.py 585L, chat_history_routes.py 63L, chat_generate_routes.py 55L) define Pydantic input models at module level and do NOT use `from __future__ import annotations`. This is the correct pattern that avoids the iter122 bug where ProjectCreate/ProjectUpdate were passed as closure args.
server.py is now 5224 lines (down from 7892 at iter120 start = -33.8%, -657 lines this round). Still above the 700-line guideline but trending strongly in the right direction.

The /chat/message endpoint correctly stayed in server.py — it uses 12 helper functions (_build_docx, _build_pdf, _build_image, _build_pptx, _build_xlsx, _build_plain, _run_python_sandbox, _context_limit, etc.) that are also entangled. Moving it would require passing all of those as factory args, which is the same trap that caused the iter122 bug. The decision to skip is sound.
The /chat/stream extraction is non-trivial (handles SSE, auto-creates a project, persists chat_messages) and works end-to-end under authentication — verified live in this run.

Suggestion (not blocking): consider extracting the message generation helpers (_build_docx/pdf/image/pptx/xlsx/plain, _run_python_sandbox) into a /app/backend/services/ module so that future extraction of /chat/message becomes safe.

Test coverage: the iter123 dedicated suite focused on unauthenticated 401 paths only, exactly the gap that masked the iter122 regression. My supplement adds two authenticated happy-paths (/chat/history, /chat/stream SSE) which catch any Pydantic body-binding or closure regression. Recommend keeping this style for future extracts.
